sourceInformation.perspective: First person on a scripted rail: sideways scroll and depth, 2.5D
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge engine 0.85.2 handoff (JavaScript, 480x270 canvas pixel buffer, E.Game, E.Arcade, E.Input, E.font, chip audio); AI Hub client 1.4.0 (session.js, unmodified); Node vm for tests; Playwright 1.63.0 for screenshots and the hub harness; single HTML bundle
sourceInformation.artDirection: Pixel art made in code: procedural depth-scaled sprites, dusk and dawn palettes
sourceInformation.animation: Procedural: soldiers rise and drop from cover, closing telegraph rings, gun recoil, pickup bob, boss weave and sway, rocket and shell flight; the engine rig system is not used
sourceInformation.audio: Engine chip synth: sound effects defined in code, voice blips for radio captions (not Animalese), engine songs for music
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub session, mode shared-world, 1-4 players: the host simulates, other copies send inputs and draw from snapshots and events; local co-op on one machine (pads join before and during an operation)
sourceInformation.testing: Node: 85 checks (unit rules, six bot playthroughs, co-op, a two-copy session through an in-process hub, scene drive-through); browser: screenshots and page errors; AI Hub harness: two-player conformance run passed
sourceInformation.research: none (used the plan's summary of the source)
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); Chromium (Playwright, headless) for screenshots

testingFeedback: About eight issues were caught in the first build, seven in the game; the expansion to six operations and co-op added more, caught by the 85 checks and by the harness run.

Two would have broken the game in a browser: the canvas size (the game drew at 300x150 with no page CSS) and the first frame running before the bot file loaded (a crash on a deep link into the attract scene). Every other issue was a visible or rule-level defect, not a crash.
Most helpful: the bot playing each operation headless to its boss, and the screenshots, which showed the canvas and layout faults the logic checks could not.
Least helpful: the stub-buffer draw pass. It shows that drawing does not throw, not that it looks right.
engineFeedback: E.Game gives the scene flow, pause menu, settings, input presets, audio and a headless loop for tests. E.Arcade gives the high-score table and initials entry for free.

Yes. The canvas stayed at its intrinsic 300x150 until I copied the template's canvas CSS; the start order (the first frame runs before later files load) cost a crash; and deep links only apply on a fresh page load.
The battle rules, the rail and beat generator, the telegraph ring logic, the depth painter for sprites (the engine's Mode 7 and rig systems were not used), the HUD, and the bot.
The API card is long, and the pixel primitives snap to whole pixels, so depth-scaled sprites needed a run-length painter of my own.
None. The engine was not changed.
A documented rule for the canvas size when a fixed res is used, and a note that the first frame can run before later script tags load.
promptFeedback: The plan's exact names, file layout, test structure and done criteria. They made the deliverables unambiguous.

The task and the plan ask for far more than one run can build (six operations, AI Hub multiplayer, local co-op, rigs, Mode 7). The plan also names a different model and effort from the task; the task won, as the plan's own order said.
Multiplayer integration with the AI Hub harness, which needs the hub's client and harness files and a session flow to test.
Split it into milestones, each with its own done line, so a run can finish one and report the rest.

aiHub.name: Operation Wolfpack
aiHub.tagline: Wolves against hyenas, one rail at a time
aiHub.description: A first-person light-gun rail shooter inspired by Operation Wolf: six operations across the Brimstone Coast, shoot the Hyena Legion, spare the civilians, and bring the workers home. Co-op for up to four in one session.
aiHub.controls: Aim with mouse or stick; hold fire to shoot; grenade on X, K or right click; R reloads; Esc pauses
